metadata.title: Rate Limits, Fixed.
metadata.note: Weekly update (changelog framing, per creator's prior choice). Narrator Muskan, @HumanitariansAI, banner 'Vendor Intelligence'. Six rate-limiting changes after a collector run stopped after 2 of 50 companies. Bookends render (composer/verdict/handoff/outro via Claude Remotion comps); body B01-B04 are house-style 4K PIL cards generated by make_cards.py. DOUBLE-CHECK LAW — exact figures from the creator's change log: run stopped after 2 of 50; 3 compounding faults; token-budget pacer (~51 lines, _await_token_budget/_record_usage, rolling 60s window, TOKENS_PER_MINUTE from GROQ_TOKENS_PER_MINUTE); retry-after parser old regex required minutes and never matched Groq's 'try again in 2.79s' → fell to 180s fallback (3s became 3min); max_attempts 2→6; throttle vs exhaustion distinguished at a 300s threshold (only real wall returns hit_rate_limit=True and stops); exhausting retries now skips one headline instead of aborting all; message was '[RATE LIMIT] Hit Groq daily limit' → now '[QUOTA] Groq quota exhausted' with a completed count; verified 10 calls ~18,000 tokens vs 8,000/min budget → waited 57s & 58s → completed 10/10, 0 abort signals, all classifications correct (previously aborted).

beats.narration_text: Hey, I'm Muskan. This morning my collector run died after just two of fifty companies. Not one bug, three, stacked on top of each other, all about rate limiting. This week was fixing them, and making the whole thing survive hitting a limit instead of falling over.

props.command: Why did the collector stop after 2 of 50 companies this morning — and how did I fix it?

beats.narration_text: Here's what actually happened. Three faults compounded. One: the retry parser never matched, so every wait became a hundred and eighty seconds instead of about three. Two: only two attempts before giving up. And three, the worst one: giving up didn't skip a headline, it aborted the entire run. Two companies in, and it was done.

show.event: the three fault cards snap in

card.title: Two of Fifty.
card.subtitle: one run, three compounding bugs

items.quote: one failure killed the whole run

card.caption: the collector stopped after 2 of 50 companies this morning

beats.narration_text: The biggest fix is a token-budget pacer. Before, the code would sprint into a call, hit a four-twenty-nine, and only then react. Now it tracks real token use in a rolling sixty-second window, and if the next call would overflow the budget, it waits first. It stops hitting the wall by not running into it.

card.title: Pace, Don't React.
card.subtitle: the token-budget pacer
card.caption: a rolling 60-second token budget (GROQ_TOKENS_PER_MINUTE) — wait before the wall, not after it
card.footer: ~51 NEW LINES · DON'T RUN INTO THE 429

beats.narration_text: Then the details. The retry parser was looking for a minutes field that Groq never sends, so its two-point-seven-nine seconds now matches, and a three second wait stays three seconds. Attempts went from two to six, since the window clears fast. A short throttle now means retry; only a long one, over three hundred seconds, counts as a real wall and stops. And a failure skips one headline instead of the whole run.

card.title: Then, the Details.
card.subtitle: four smaller fixes
card.caption: the retry-after regex required a minutes field Groq never sends

beats.narration_text: Does it work? I ran ten calls, about eighteen thousand tokens, against an eight thousand per minute budget. The pacer waited fifty-seven seconds, then fifty-eight, and finished all ten, with zero abort signals, and every classification correct. The exact run that fell over this morning now paces itself and completes.

show.event: the load and budget feed the pacer

card.title: Verified.
card.subtitle: the run that died this morning
card.caption: previously this aborted; now it paces and finishes the run

beats.narration_text: The theme: pace ahead of the limit instead of reacting to it, read the real wait instead of guessing, and when you do hit a wall, skip one thing and keep going, don't abandon the job. And say what's actually true in the logs.

props.artifactHeading: Why the run died, and what changed
artifactLines: Stopped after 2 of 50 — three faults: a broken retry parser, only 2 attempts, and abort-on-failure.
New: a token-budget pacer waits before a call would overflow the 60-second window (not after a 429).
Parser fixed (“2.79s” → 3s, not a 180s fallback); attempts 2 → 6; seconds-throttle vs a real wall (>300s).
Failures skip one headline, not all 50; the run message now reports quota honestly, with a completed count.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Find one retry or backoff in your own code. When it finally gives up, does it fail the whole job, or just skip that one item and keep going? And is it reacting to limits after it hits them, or pacing ahead so it doesn't? Those two choices are the difference between a run that finishes and one that dies at item two.

props.command: Find one retry/backoff in my code. When it gives up, does it fail the whole job or skip one item and continue? And does it react to limits, or pace ahead of them?
output: parse the real wait, don't guess

beats.narration_text: Rate limits, fixed. Pace ahead, and degrade gracefully. Humanitarians AI.
